clue.text: Influence dance music

definitions.meaning: to sway or affect someone, as a speech may shift voters
jazz with a strong lilting rhythm, played for big-band dancing in the 1930s and 1940s

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on how much dance music shapes things.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to sway an outcome, and the big-band jazz style made for dancing.

clue.text: Convert upsetting a sacred book

indicators.note: convert means change into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A convert is distressing a holy text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' looks like a noun (a new believer) but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Septuagint is the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament, a sacred text.

clue.text: European river providing watering-hole

definitions.meaning: a river flowing from Switzerland through Austria into the Danube
a pub, a place to drink

explanation.surface: A river in Europe supplies a place to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the Alpine river through Innsbruck, and a pub where people drink.

clue.text: Transparently smooth guy heartlessly taking girl in

indicators.note: taking ... in means holding inside, so one piece goes into the other
in completes taking in, putting the girl inside
heartlessly means the middle letter is removed, keeping the outside

parts.note: lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A slick fellow callously lures a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' strips the middle letter of the guy word; 'taking ... in' is split around 'girl', which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Glassy describes a surface smooth and clear like glass, so transparently smooth.

clue.text: So-called lady, in part liberal

definitions.meaning: Lady ... is a stage role, the generous lady in Farquhar's play The Beaux' Stratagem, so the lady is so called in a part

explanation.surface: A supposed lady who is only partly broad-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in part' means in a theatrical role: Lady Bountiful is the charitable character in George Farquhar's comedy The Beaux' Stratagem, whose name became a byword.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal here means generous and giving freely, which is the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Erected defence as writer's protecting villain

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the writer goes round the villain

parts.note: J M Barrie, author of Peter Pan
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A defence put up because an author shields a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a barrier hastily set up for defence, so a defence that has been erected.

clue.text: Discourage fellow in international organization

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man in a world body is disheartened.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to drain their courage, a synonym of dishearten or discourage.

clue.text: Binary digital signal successfully received

parts.note: binary means two and digital refers to fingers, so a signal made with a pair of digits meaning all is well

explanation.surface: A computer's binary signal has arrived intact.
explanation.walkthrough: Digital puns on digits as fingers: a gesture of two digits that says message received, all fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-handed gesture with raised thumbs signals approval or that something went well.

clue.text: Catholic expert on mysteries of death

definitions.text: Catholic expert on mysteries of death

parts.words: Catholic expert on mysteries of death
parts.note: a priest whose expertise seems religious mystery turns out to be solving murders in G K Chesterton's stories

explanation.surface: A Catholic theologian who specialises in the mysteries of mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: The mysteries sound theological but are detective stories: Chesterton's priest-detective solves murders.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's fictional Catholic priest is an amateur detective who solves killings.

clue.text: King Edward, the humorist

definitions.meaning: the Shakespearean monarch of ancient Britain
Edward of that surname wrote nonsense verse and limericks

explanation.surface: King Edward is the comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' reads as a monarch but splits: Shakespeare's king, and Edward Lear the nonsense poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: Shakespeare's tragic king, and Edward the Victorian writer of limericks.

clue.text: Mystical symbol, quotation, and sign by author

parts.note: pen stands for a writer, as in a hired pen
a tag is a well-known quotation, often Latin
the Ram is Aries, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A list of a mystic's emblem, a quote and an author's sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' places the author piece next to the other two; it comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star used in magic and occultism is a classic mystical emblem.

clue.text: Extremist contributing to hateful traditions

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fanatic helps keep nasty customs alive.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, a noun synonym for an extremist.

clue.text: Is half a bun one cooked out now?

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or messed about with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a half-bun that has been baked has gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the anagram signal working on IS HALF A BUN ONE, all thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer in fashion is out, and out now is a phrase for currently passe.

clue.text: In order to get fabric, I am in Scottish town

parts.note: for means in order to, as in done for money
twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribs
taken as written

explanation.surface: To get cloth, I am in a Highland town.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort William is a town in the Scottish Highlands near Ben Nevis.

clue.text: One provides security for an advance from bank

definitions.text: One provides security for an advance
definitions.meaning: a foothold won by troops that protects their further advance
the end of a bridge on a river bank

explanation.surface: Someone guarantees a loan advanced from a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Security for an advance and bank look like money lending, but both senses are military and riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a foothold that secures a military advance, and the end of a bridge at the bank.

clue.text: Maid serving American sides

parts.note: a GI is an American serviceman
right and left, abbreviated R and L, are the two sides

explanation.surface: A housemaid waits on US visitors at either side of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid is an old word for a young unmarried woman, a synonym in the older sense.

clue.text: Net, for example? Square type

definitions.meaning: net is the number ten written backwards, so it is a number read back

explanation.surface: Is a net an example of a square pattern?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful first sense: NET is TEN reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A back number is a person seen as old-fashioned, which is what a square is in slang.

clue.text: Coiling about big rock, an enormous snake

indicators.note: coiling about means twisting round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge snake winds itself round a large boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coiling about' is the anagram signal on BIG ROCK AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The king cobra is the longest venomous snake, so an enormous snake.

clue.text: Unusually stern father missing the player's move

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so these letters are rearranged
missing means without, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: A dad, oddly stern, misses the footballer's change of club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing the' takes THE out of FATHER to leave FAR; 'Unusually' rearranges STERN and FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfer is a player's move from one club to another.

clue.text: Information about gold not plentiful in port

indicators.note: about means going round, so the information word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: news is information
or is gold in heraldry
lean means meagre, not plentiful

explanation.surface: Reports say gold is in short supply at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louisiana city is a major Mississippi river port, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Concert promoter would, for listeners

indicators.note: for listeners means the word is taken as it is heard, not as it is spelt

parts.note: the word would, taken as said

explanation.surface: A concert organiser says he would, for the audience's sake.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Wood founded the London Promenade Concerts, the Proms, in 1895.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wood founded and conducted the Proms, so he is a famous promoter of concerts.

clue.text: French language class in British school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A French lesson in a British school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class in' links the pieces: Eton is a well-known English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton is the Celtic language spoken in Brittany in north-west France.

clue.text: Fearing, in cult, crazy extremists

indicators.note: crazy means wildly disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Extremists inside a cult are full of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' signals the anagram of FEARING IN CULT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the wild, fanatical minority on the edge of a movement, a synonym for extremists.

clue.text: Mark in American literature that was a low number

definitions.meaning: the pen name Mark of Samuel Clemens, the author of Huckleberry Finn

explanation.surface: A mark in American literature that once scored low.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the author of Tom Sawyer, and the archaic word meaning two.

clue.text: Covers up swindle

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: macs are raincoats, coverings

explanation.surface: Someone hides a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people, a synonym for a swindle.

clue.text: Ordinary type in charge

definitions.meaning: in heraldry an ordinary is a simple charge, and the band across the top of a shield is one of them

explanation.surface: An average sort of person is put in command.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry the 'ordinaries' are the basic charges on a shield; the top band is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a heraldic band across a shield's top, and the head person in command.

clue.text: Decide a right measure of computer's speed

parts.note: bit rate measures how fast data is transferred, in bits per second

explanation.surface: Settle on a correct measure for how fast a computer runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to judge a dispute and settle it, so to decide.

clue.text: Division ready for war

definitions.meaning: a branch or section of an organisation

explanation.surface: A part of the army prepared for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a branch of an organisation, and to equip with weapons ready for fighting.

clue.text: Records in golf club set by me and doctor

parts.note: taken as written
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
the R and A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews

explanation.surface: Records at a golf club are set by me and a medic.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and A at St Andrews is golf's historic governing club; 'set by' puts it after the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written notes kept for reference, so records in the plural.

clue.text: Entitled to state requirements, mostly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read in the other direction
mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: to demand is to state what one requires

explanation.surface: A person feels entitled to list demands that are largely turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of DEMAND to leave DEMAN, and 'rejected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Named means given a name or title, so entitled in the sense of called.
